I have what I need. The primary sources were reachable for everything that matters except the twin.

REJECTED

The build itself is clean — I verified by md5, not mtime, that `main.pdf` was built from the exact current `main.tex`, `circumplex_subsection.tex`, and `substrate_independence_section.tex` (hashes in `main.fdb_latexmk` lines 143/147/148 match the files on disk). No stale PDF, no undefined citations, no orphaned bib entries (13 used, 13 defined). The problems are in the claims.

---

## CRITICAL

**1. A retracted finding is still filed under "Confirmed," and the count of 8 depends on it.**
`main.tex:607` — "The full audited record comprises 8~confirmed findings". The canonical source is `archive/meta-pattern/main.tex:148`:

> `User emotion encoding & Confirmed & Meta & $2.5$--$2.8\times$ at L3--L4 \\`

That row sits under `\multicolumn{4}{l}{\textit{Confirmed (8) --- all metacognitive state}}`. But this paper's own footnote (`main.tex:188-198`) says that exact figure "was retracted at its source on 2026-05-21 as an FWL-before-CV leakage artifact" and that "the spectral probe for emotion is at chance." The retracted number also still appears at `meta-pattern/main.tex:170` (`Discrete emotion & Suspected & Meta & 2.5--2.8× chance`).

This is the known kill, verbatim: a retraction propagated into prose in one edition and never re-filed in the status table. The convergence paper inherits `8` from a table whose eighth row it has itself retracted.
**Fix:** re-file the row as Falsified with the leakage reason, change the count to **7 confirmed**, and propagate to `meta-pattern`'s abstract ("8 confirmed"), intro (line 94), the split table (line 187, `8/8`), and the "8-for-8 on metacognition" claim at line 50.

**2. The FWL label is inverted between the two documents on the headline AUROC.**
This paper (abstract, `main.tex:181`, `main.tex:310`): AUROC **0.620 after** FWL, **0.707 without** FWL.
`meta-pattern/main.tex:141`: `Confabulation detection & Confirmed & Meta & AUROC 0.707 (FWL)`.
Both cannot be true. If this paper is right, the canonical table's top confirmed finding is labeled with the leakage-inflated number presented as the corrected one.
**Fix:** resolve against the decision-state fold-level outputs and correct whichever document is wrong. I could not adjudicate this from either document — flagged again under "could not check."

**3. The abstract's "80–100% deception correction" is not in the source, and it suppresses a failed pre-registered endpoint.**
Primary: `archive/targeted-deception-correction/paper.md:13`. The actual result is an exploratory N=20 proof where deception goes **from an 80% baseline to 0%**, plus a pre-registered confirmatory replication (N=30, novel frames) with a 30% baseline that **did not meet its primary endpoint (p=0.34)**; only the placebo comparison held (p=0.019). No "80–100%" range exists anywhere in the source — it reads as the 80% baseline fused with the 20/20 (100%) capability-preservation figure.

§2.2 does disclose p=0.34. The abstract does not, and the abstract is the venue-facing claim.
**Fix:** abstract to read "complete correction of an 80% baseline deception rate in an exploratory proof (N=20); a pre-registered confirmatory replication with novel frames did not meet its primary endpoint (p=0.34), with the placebo comparison remaining significant (p=0.019)." Same correction at `main.tex:314` and `substrate_independence_section.tex:310`.

**4. The same result is "deception" in one file and "confabulation" in the other — and the bib title says confabulation.**
`main.tex` says "deception correction" four times (abstract:69, 185, 204, 314). `substrate_independence_section.tex:310` says "(80--100\% **confabulation** correction)". `references.bib:86` titles the cited work "The Oracle Loop: Real-Time **Confabulation** Detection via KV-Cache Geometry" — but the artifact it points to is the targeted-deception-correction paper (L35–L47 steering, matching `main.tex:204` exactly).

This is not cosmetic. The paper's AST argument at `main.tex:709-711` rests on confabulation and deception having *opposite* spectral signatures ("spectral contraction (confabulation) and expansion (deception)"). Using the labels interchangeably for the same number breaks that argument.
**Fix:** "deception" throughout; correct the `lyra2026oracle` bib title to the actual paper title.

**5. The paper's strongest AST claim is falsified by its own falsification list.**
`main.tex:610-611`: "The falsified findings all attempted content-level measurement." Restated at `main.tex:684-687` as "the strongest alignment."

Its own list two sentences later (`main.tex:617-624`): RLHF miscalibration thesis (a *calibration* claim), workspace-noise framing (a *spectral state* claim), and the "3×" tail ratio (a *spectral state* claim). Three of the four listed falsifications are state-level, not content-level. Only cache-tracing observational alignment is content.

The canonical 10 in `meta-pattern` *are* all Content — which is why this paper says "10**+**". The "+" is absorbing exactly the falsifications that break the split, and it desyncs the count from the canonical `10`.
**Fix:** either fold the sprint falsifications into the table and retire the "every falsified finding is content" claim, or state an explicit inclusion criterion for why they are excluded from the tally. Do not ship the "+".

---

## MAJOR

**6.** `main.tex:529-532` — "the stable rank *peak* occurs at $L{=}19$ ($30.2\%$ depth), within the convergence paper's $31$--$33\%$ band." Two defects: 30.2% is **not** within 31–33%; and "the convergence paper's" is a self-reference — this *is* the convergence paper, un-revoiced from a standalone R-series report. **Fix:** "at 30.2% depth, just below the 31–33% band reported in §3.1."

**7.** Depth denominators disagree. `substrate_independence_section.tex:151` declares relative depth as $l/n_\text{layers}$ (=/64, giving L21→33%). §6 uses /63 (L19→30.2%, L14→22.2%, L56.2→89%). Under /64 the mechanism peak is 29.7%, further from the band. **Fix:** declare one convention in Experimental Setup and recompute.

**8.** `main.tex:838-840`: "Generation used temperature${=}0$ (greedy)" with no hedge, contradicting the primary mechanism experiment at `main.tex:421-422`: "5~temperature-sampled forks each ($T{=}0.7$, seeded)". **Fix:** scope the greedy statement, and state T=0.7 as the documented exception.

**9.** `main.tex:448-454` ("Architecture-phase control") and `main.tex:491-502` ("Architectural qualification") report the identical result — 14.5 layers [11.7–17.4], 81% forks positive — twice in the same subsection. **Fix:** delete the first; the second carries the interpretation.

**10.** `main.tex:833-835`: "seven additional models: Qwen2.5-0.6B through Qwen2.5-72B". Qwen2.5 has no 0.6B checkpoint (0.5B is the smallest; 0.6B is Qwen3), and 72B contradicts the "$0.6$B--$70$B" claimed at `main.tex:60` and `main.tex:247`. "Seven" is also not enumerable from the text. **Fix:** list all seven model IDs explicitly and make the range in the abstract match them.

**11.** `main.tex:329` calls L15 "workspace-band depth" in a subsection that specifies Qwen3-8B (`main.tex:339`). L15/36 = 41.7%, outside the paper's 31–33% band and well past the 8B local max at L12. The model for the decomposition is never stated in that subsection. **Fix:** name the model and justify L15 against whichever band definition you are using.

**12.** Oracle Loop layer set is internally inconsistent. `main.tex:203-204` says it operates "at the materialization boundary (L35--L47)"; `substrate_independence_section.tex:302-303` says it "detects at L27, L31, L35, L39, L43 and L47 and **corrects at L11**." The primary source (`targeted-deception-correction/paper.md:13`) describes correction as "steering late-layer (L35-L47) activations." The L11 claim carries an interpretive paragraph (`:312-315`, "roughly 17% depth --- well before the 33% dimensionality maximum") that collapses if L11 is wrong. All seven cited layers are correctly ≡3 mod 4, so the full-attention arithmetic is sound — it's the correction layer that's unsourced. **Fix:** reconcile against the Oracle harness config and cite it.

**13.** `main.tex:632-634` cites the Mistral text-baseline result to `lyra2026decision`. The numbers are correct — I verified 0.820 and 0.806 at `dual-detector-paper/main.tex:318,322,330` — but they live in the **dual-detector paper**, which has no entry in `references.bib`. `ACTIVE_REVIEW.md:53` separately flags that paper as unreviewed and previously cited while housed only in a deprecated repo. **Fix:** add the dual-detector bib entry and re-point the citation.

**14.** `circumplex_subsection.tex:14-15`: "peaking at near-identity ($d = 0.987$)". This is a cosine, but `$d$` denotes Cohen's d everywhere else in the paper (d=2.35, d=0.91, d=1.85, d=0.684). **Fix:** `$\cos = 0.987$`.

**15.** `main.tex:38`: `\date{July 2026}` on a document containing a "Corrected 2026-08-14" footnote and an August-2026 section revision. The visible date contradicts the visible correction. **Fix:** `\date{August 2026}` plus a revision line.

**16.** The body count is asserted but never enumerated — no confirmed findings listed, only 4 of "10+" falsifications. For a paper whose thesis *is* the body count, and given that the known failure mode is a row filed under the wrong heading, this makes the defect class undetectable by construction. **Fix:** reproduce `meta-pattern`'s `tab:bodycount` with an explicit Status column so the two editions can be diffed mechanically.

---

## MINOR

**20.** `main.tex:875` — "archived on Zenodo" with no DOI.
**21.** `main.tex:182` — "range $0.620$--$0.999$ across designs" leaves 0.999 unattributed to any design; as written it reads as headroom-shopping in a paper that otherwise polices this well.
**22.** `main.blg` — "Warning--empty journal in gurnee2026gwt". It is `@article` with no journal. Use `@misc` with the Transformer Circuits note.
**23.** Nine overfull hboxes; worst are 39.6pt (lines 420–425) and 37.3pt (838–841).
**24.** Contributions appear only inside a first-person shaded box (`main.tex:118-122`). A venue will want a formal Author Contributions section.
**25.** `main.tex:632` says text features "matched" the detector at 0.820 vs 0.806 — text features slightly *exceeded* it. The source (`dual-detector-paper:330`) also says "match," so this is inherited, but "matched or slightly exceeded" is the honest phrasing.
